# 12-Week Prenatal Strength Programme

**Client Profile:** 30-year-old advanced lifter, 20 weeks pregnant at programme start, finishing at ~32 weeks. OB-cleared for moderate strength training.

## Programming Principles

Given she'll progress from second trimester into late third trimester, this programme is structured as a **gradual deload**, not a build. We maintain strength and movement quality while autoregulating intensity downward as the pregnancy advances. RPE caps drop each phase. All work is in the 5-8 RPE range — never grinding reps, always 2-4 reps in reserve.

**Universal modifications throughout:**
- No supine work beyond 30 seconds (incline bench minimum 15°)
- No Valsalva — exhale on exertion
- Monitor for diastasis recti; regress if doming appears
- Stop on: dizziness, contractions, leaking fluid, bleeding, persistent pain, reduced fetal movement
- Hydration and core temperature priorities
- RPE caps: Phase 1 = 7, Phase 2 = 6, Phase 3 = 5

**Weekly structure:** 4 sessions — Lower A, Upper A, Lower B, Upper B

---

## PHASE 1: WEEKS 1–4 (Pregnancy weeks 20–23)
*Focus: Establish prenatal-adapted patterns, maintain strength baseline*

### Lower A
- Goblet box squat (above parallel) — 4×6 @ RPE 7
- Trap bar RDL — 4×8 @ RPE 7
- DB reverse lunge — 3×8/leg
- Single-leg glute bridge — 3×10/leg
- Side plank — 3×30s/side

### Upper A
- Incline DB bench press (30°) — 4×8 @ RPE 7
- Chest-supported row — 4×8
- Half-kneeling landmine press — 3×8/side
- Seated cable row, neutral grip — 3×10
- Pallof press — 3×10/side

### Lower B
- Front-foot-elevated split squat — 4×8/leg
- Hip thrust (shoulders on bench, neutral spine) — 4×8 @ RPE 7
- Step-up to box — 3×8/leg
- Hamstring curl (seated or standing) — 3×10
- Bird dog — 3×8/side

### Upper B
- Neutral-grip lat pulldown — 4×8
- Landmine press, standing — 4×8/side
- Single-arm DB row — 3×10/side
- Cable face pull — 3×12
- Dead bug (regress if doming) — 3×8/side

**Weekly progression:** Add 1 rep or small load each week, RPE never exceeds 7.

---

## PHASE 2: WEEKS 5–8 (Pregnancy weeks 24–27)
*Focus: Reduce spinal loading, increase unilateral work, shift to higher reps*

### Lower A
- Heels-elevated goblet squat — 3×10 @ RPE 6
- Single-leg RDL (DBs, supported as needed) — 3×8/leg
- Walking lunge (DBs) — 3×10/leg
- Cable pull-through — 3×12
- Copenhagen plank regression — 3×20s/side

### Upper A
- Incline DB bench (45°) — 3×10 @ RPE 6
- Seated cable row — 3×10
- DB Z-press (seated upright) — 3×10
- Single-arm half-kneeling lat pulldown — 3×10/side
- Pallof press iso-hold — 3×20s/side

### Lower B
- Belt squat or hack squat (knee-friendly) — 3×10 @ RPE 6
- B-stance hip thrust — 3×10/leg
- Reverse lunge from deficit — 3×8/leg (remove deficit if balance off)
- Seated leg curl — 3×12
- Side plank with leg lift — 3×8/side

### Upper B
- Neutral-grip pulldown — 3×10
- Half-kneeling single-arm landmine press — 3×10/side
- Chest-supported T-bar row — 3×10
- Cable rear delt fly — 3×12
- Standing cable anti-rotation — 3×10/side

**Progression note:** Loads may need to plateau or reduce by mid-Phase 2 as belly size affects mechanics. Stance widens; squat depth reduces naturally — that's fine.

---

## PHASE 3: WEEKS 9–12 (Pregnancy weeks 28–31)
*Focus: Movement maintenance, labour-prep conditioning, postural support, fatigue management*

### Lower A
- Goblet squat to box (parallel or above) — 3×8 @ RPE 5
- Cable pull-through — 3×12
- DB step-up — 3×8/leg
- Seated leg curl — 3×12
- Deep squat hold (supported) — 3×30s

### Upper A
- Incline DB bench (45°) — 3×8 @ RPE 5
- Seated cable row — 3×12
- Half-kneeling landmine press — 3×8/side
- Single-arm pulldown — 3×10/side
- Diaphragmatic breathing drills — 3×8 breaths

### Lower B
- Hip thrust (light load, focus on glute connection) — 3×10
- Single-leg glute bridge — 3×10/leg
- Wall sit — 3×30s
- Banded clamshells — 3×15/side
- Cat-camel — 3×8

### Upper B
- Chest-supported row — 3×10
- DB Arnold press (light) — 3×10
- Face pull — 3×15
- Band pull-apart — 3×15
- Side-lying breathing with pelvic floor coordination — 3×8

**Final two weeks (11–12):** Drop one set across the board. Add 5–10 min of low-intensity walking or stationary bike at session end. Prioritise mobility — hip openers, thoracic rotations, ankle work.

---

## Recovery & Session Management

- **Warm-up (10 min every session):** cat-camel, 90/90 breathing, hip CARs, banded glute activation, scap work
- **Cool-down (5–8 min):** pelvic floor breathing, hip flexor stretch, child's pose variation
- **Session duration:** Cap at 60 min Phase 1, 50 min Phase 2, 45 min Phase 3
- **Rest periods:** 90–120s between working sets — she should never feel breathless
- **Talk test:** She must be able to hold a conversation throughout
- **Sleep:** Encourage left-side sleeping, pillow support; programme around her energy

## Red Flags — Stop Session Immediately
Vaginal bleeding, fluid leak, contractions, dizziness, chest pain, calf swelling/pain, headache, reduced fetal movement, abdominal doming that doesn't resolve with cueing.

## Communication Cadence
Check in with her OB or midwife if anything changes — pelvic girdle pain, SPD, gestational diabetes, blood pressure issues. Reassess the programme at any growth scan or appointment that changes her clearance.

Let me know if you want me to layer in a postpartum return-to-lifting protocol for after her 6-week clearance, or adjust any phase based on how she's tolerating the work.

# Prenatal Nutrition Plan — Maintaining Lean Mass

**Important caveat:** Nutrition during pregnancy should be coordinated with her OB, midwife, or a prenatal-specialised RD, especially if she has gestational diabetes risk, anaemia, hyperemesis, or any flagged bloods. This is a framework for a healthy, OB-cleared, training client — not medical advice. Flag anything unusual to her care team.

---

## Caloric Framework

She's 20 weeks at programme start, finishing around 32 weeks — spanning mid-second to late-third trimester. Energy needs increase as pregnancy progresses, and underfeeding an advanced lifter who's still training 4x/week will cost her lean mass and energy.

**Baseline approach (above pre-pregnancy maintenance):**
- **Weeks 1–4 (preg weeks 20–23, 2nd trimester):** +340 kcal/day over pre-pregnancy maintenance
- **Weeks 5–12 (preg weeks 24–31, 3rd trimester):** +450 kcal/day over pre-pregnancy maintenance

If pre-pregnancy maintenance is unknown, estimate using current bodyweight: ~30–32 kcal/kg of pre-pregnancy weight, then add the trimester surplus.

**Weight gain target (IOM guidelines, normal pre-pregnancy BMI):** 11.5–16 kg total, roughly 0.4–0.5 kg/week in 2nd and 3rd trimesters. Track trend, not daily fluctuations. If gain stalls or exceeds the range over a 3-week trend, adjust intake by ±200 kcal.

---

## Macronutrient Targets

**Protein: 1.6–1.8 g/kg of current bodyweight**
This is well above standard prenatal recommendations and is the single most important lever for maintaining lean mass while training. Recent prenatal research supports intakes in this range as safe and likely optimal for active women. Distribute across 4–5 feedings of 30–40 g each — leucine threshold matters more in pregnancy due to nutrient partitioning toward the fetus.

**Carbohydrates: 4–5 g/kg**
Supports training output, fetal glucose demand, and prevents ketosis (which should be avoided during pregnancy). Skew toward whole-food sources. Bump pre- and post-training feeds.

**Fat: 0.8–1.0 g/kg, minimum**
Critical for fetal brain development and hormone production. Emphasise omega-3s (especially DHA).

---

## Meal Structure

A 4–5 meal pattern works best — large meals become uncomfortable in the third trimester as the uterus crowds the stomach, and reflux is common.

**Sample day (scale portions to her bodyweight):**

**Breakfast**
- 3 whole eggs + 1 extra white, scrambled
- 60g oats with berries, Greek yoghurt, ground flax
- Coffee (cap caffeine at 200 mg/day total)

**Mid-morning snack**
- 200g cottage cheese or Skyr with walnuts and honey

**Pre-training meal (60–90 min out)**
- 150g chicken or salmon
- 200g rice or potato
- Cooked vegetables, olive oil

**Post-training**
- 40g whey isolate (third-party tested) + banana
- Or: tuna sandwich on sourdough with avocado

**Dinner**
- 180g lean beef, salmon, or tofu
- Sweet potato or quinoa
- Large mixed salad with olive oil and seeds

**Evening (optional, helps with sleep and overnight protein)**
- Greek yoghurt with nut butter and chia, or casein shake

---

## Key Micronutrients

A **prenatal multivitamin is non-negotiable** — assume she's on one, but verify it contains:

- **Folate (as methylfolate or folic acid):** 600 mcg
- **Iron:** 27 mg — pair non-heme sources with vitamin C; iron needs spike in trimester 3
- **Choline:** 450 mg — most prenatals under-dose this. Eggs, liver, soy. Critically important for fetal brain development and often under-consumed
- **DHA/EPA:** 300+ mg DHA daily — fatty fish 2x/week or algae-based supplement. Limit high-mercury fish (tuna steak, swordfish, king mackerel)
- **Iodine:** 220 mcg
- **Vitamin D:** 600–2000 IU depending on status — get her levels checked
- **Calcium:** 1000 mg, mostly from food
- **B12:** especially if she's vegetarian/vegan

**Foods to emphasise daily:**
- Eggs (choline, protein)
- Greek yoghurt, kefir (protein, calcium, probiotics)
- Leafy greens (folate, iron, magnesium)
- Berries (antioxidants, fibre)
- Fatty fish 2x/week (salmon, sardines)
- Lentils, beans (iron, fibre, folate)
- Nuts and seeds (fats, magnesium, zinc)
- Liver 1x/week if she tolerates it (choline, iron, B12, vitamin A — cap at 75g/week due to retinol)

---

## Foods to Avoid or Limit

- Raw/undercooked fish, eggs, meat
- Unpasteurised dairy and soft cheeses
- Deli meats unless heated through (listeria risk)
- High-mercury fish (swordfish, king mackerel, marlin, shark, large tuna)
- Alcohol (zero)
- Caffeine over 200 mg/day
- Excess liver/retinol (>75g liver per week)
- Raw sprouts
- Unwashed produce

---

## Training Day Nutrition

**Pre-training (60–90 min before):** Mixed meal with 30–40g protein, 50–80g carbs, moderate fat. Avoid training fasted — blood sugar regulation is more volatile in pregnancy.

**Intra-training:** Sip 500–750 ml water with a pinch of salt. If sessions feel hard or she's lightheaded, add 20–30g carbs (sports drink, dates) mid-session — fetal glucose demand is real.

**Post-training (within 60 min):** 30–40g protein + 60–80g carbs. This window matters more than usual given the catabolic pressure of fetal demand.

**Hydration:** 3–3.5 L/day baseline, more in hot weather or on training days. Dehydration can trigger contractions. Urine should be pale straw colour.

---

## Phase-Specific Adjustments

**Programme Weeks 1–4 (preg 20–23):**
Energy generally good. Set the habits now. Aim for the full protein target. Watch for iron-deficiency symptoms (fatigue, breathlessness) — blood volume is expanding rapidly.

**Programme Weeks 5–8 (preg 24–27):**
Heartburn and reflux often start. Move to 5 smaller meals. Avoid lying down within 90 min of eating. Reduce spicy/acidic foods if symptomatic. Glucose tolerance test happens around preg week 24–28 — adjust carb distribution if any gestational diabetes flags appear (smaller, more frequent carb feeds, paired with protein and fat).

**Programme Weeks 9–12 (preg 28–31):**
Stomach capacity drops noticeably. 5–6 mini-meals. Front-load protein earlier in the day when appetite is better. Constipation often worsens — 30+ g fibre, plenty of water, magnesium glycinate may help (clear with OB). Leg cramps respond well to magnesium, potassium, and hydration.

---

## Lean Mass Preservation — Key Levers

In order of impact:

1. **Hit the protein target every single day.** Non-negotiable. This is the dominant variable.
2. **Don't undereat.** Surplus is required. Fear of weight gain causes muscle loss.
3. **Distribute protein across 4–5 feedings**, each hitting 30g+.
4. **Prioritise post-training feeding** within 60 min.
5. **Sleep 8+ hours** — third trimester sleep is hard; left-side, pillow support, magnesium pre-bed.
6. **Keep training stimulus** as programmed — undereating + reduced loading = accelerated lean mass loss.

---

## Monitoring

Weekly check-ins should track:
- Bodyweight trend (weekly average, not daily)
- Energy in sessions (1–10)
- Sleep quality
- Bowel regularity
- Any swelling, headaches, visual changes — escalate to OB immediately
- Appetite — sudden drops can signal an issue

Let me know if you want me to build a postpartum nutrition transition (lactation adds 400–500 kcal and shifts hydration and micronutrient needs significantly), or a vegetarian/vegan version of this plan.

# 12-Week Prenatal Cardio Programme

Cardio in pregnancy is genuinely beneficial — it supports cardiovascular adaptation to expanding blood volume, helps glucose regulation, reduces gestational hypertension risk, improves sleep, and is associated with shorter labours and faster postpartum recovery. ACOG recommends 150+ min/week of moderate cardio for uncomplicated pregnancies.

For an advanced lifter with OB clearance, we can be more structured than the general guidelines suggest — but the principles still apply: **moderate intensity, no overheating, no breath-holding, listen to the body.**

---

## Intensity Guidance

We're not using max HR formulas — they're unreliable in pregnancy due to elevated resting HR and blood volume changes. Use these instead:

- **Talk test (primary tool):** She should be able to hold a conversation in full sentences. If she can only speak in short phrases, back off.
- **RPE 4–6 on a 1–10 scale** for steady-state work
- **RPE 7 cap** for any intervals — never above
- **Borg 6–20 scale:** stay in the 12–14 range

**Hard caps:**
- No work above ventilatory threshold
- No sessions above 45 min of continuous moderate cardio in Phase 3
- Core temp must stay under 38.5°C — no hot rooms, no saunas, no peak-summer outdoor sessions
- Avoid supine cardio (no flat-back rowing machine setup if she leans back significantly — upright is fine)

---

## Modality Selection

**Green light (low impact, controlled):**
- Stationary bike (upright or recumbent — recumbent gets better as belly grows)
- Elliptical
- Incline walking on treadmill
- Swimming and aquatic work (excellent — reduces joint load, helps swelling)
- Stairmaster at moderate pace
- Rowing machine (upright posture, monitor as belly grows — likely drop by Phase 3)

**Yellow light (assess and monitor):**
- Outdoor walking/hiking (terrain, balance, heat)
- Light jogging (only if she was a runner pre-pregnancy and it remains comfortable — most stop by trimester 3 due to pelvic floor pressure and SPD risk)

**Red light:**
- HIIT in the traditional sense
- Anything with fall risk (road cycling, trail running)
- Contact or collision activities
- Altitude work
- Hot yoga, hot pilates

---

## Weekly Cardio Structure

Cardio sits **alongside** the strength programme, not replacing it. Total weekly cardio: **150–180 min**, split across 4–5 sessions.

**Weekly template:**
- 2 strength + cardio combo days (short cardio post-lift)
- 2 dedicated cardio days (one steady-state, one interval or mixed)
- 1 active recovery day (walk or swim)

---

## PHASE 1: WEEKS 1–4 (Preg weeks 20–23)

**Goal:** Establish aerobic base, build session tolerance.

| Day | Session |
|-----|---------|
| Mon | Lower A + 15 min easy bike (RPE 4) |
| Tue | **Cardio:** 30 min steady incline walk @ RPE 5–6 |
| Wed | Upper A + 10 min elliptical cooldown |
| Thu | **Cardio intervals:** 5 min warm-up, then 6 × (2 min @ RPE 6 / 2 min @ RPE 3) on bike, 5 min cooldown = 34 min |
| Fri | Lower B + 15 min easy bike |
| Sat | Upper B + 10 min walk |
| Sun | **Active recovery:** 30–40 min walk or easy swim @ RPE 3–4 |

**Total: ~160 min cardio**

---

## PHASE 2: WEEKS 5–8 (Preg weeks 24–27)

**Goal:** Maintain volume, shift toward lower-impact modalities, reduce interval intensity.

| Day | Session |
|-----|---------|
| Mon | Lower A + 15 min recumbent bike (RPE 4) |
| Tue | **Cardio:** 35 min — alternate 5 min bike / 5 min elliptical @ RPE 5 |
| Wed | Upper A + 10 min elliptical |
| Thu | **Cardio intervals (reduced):** 5 min warm-up, then 5 × (90s @ RPE 6 / 2:30 @ RPE 3) on bike or elliptical, 5 min cooldown = 30 min |
| Fri | Lower B + 15 min walk or bike |
| Sat | Upper B + 10 min elliptical |
| Sun | **Active recovery:** 30 min swim or aquatic walking |

**Total: ~155 min cardio**

**Notes for Phase 2:**
- Swimming becomes increasingly valuable — encourage it
- Switch to recumbent bike if upright becomes uncomfortable on the perineum/pelvis
- Drop intervals entirely if she's fatigued or sleep is poor — swap for steady-state
- Monitor for round ligament pain — common around preg week 24–28

---

## PHASE 3: WEEKS 9–12 (Preg weeks 28–31)

**Goal:** Maintain aerobic conditioning with minimal strain. Shift toward labour-prep conditioning.

| Day | Session |
|-----|---------|
| Mon | Lower A + 10 min recumbent bike (RPE 4) |
| Tue | **Cardio:** 30 min — recumbent bike or aquatic walking @ RPE 4–5 |
| Wed | Upper A + 10 min elliptical |
| Thu | **Cardio:** 30 min — split bike/elliptical, all steady @ RPE 5 (no intervals) |
| Fri | Lower B + 10 min walk |
| Sat | Upper B + 10 min easy bike |
| Sun | **Active recovery:** 30–40 min swim or walk @ RPE 3 |

**Total: ~140 min cardio**

**Final two weeks (11–12):**
- Drop one cardio session if fatigue accumulates
- Replace any uncomfortable modality with swimming or aquatic walking
- Add daily 10–15 min easy walks if tolerated — supports digestion, sleep, and labour prep
- Introduce **prenatal-specific breathing work** (5 min daily): diaphragmatic breathing, pelvic floor coordination — directly transfers to labour

---

## Session Monitoring Checklist

Before every cardio session, she should be able to answer **yes** to all:
- Slept reasonably?
- Eaten in the last 2–3 hours?
- Hydrated?
- No unusual symptoms today (swelling, headache, reduced fetal movement)?

During session, **stop immediately for:**
- Dizziness or lightheadedness
- Chest pain or palpitations beyond mild elevation
- Headache that develops mid-session
- Calf pain or swelling (DVT risk is elevated in pregnancy)
- Vaginal bleeding or fluid
- Contractions
- Sudden reduced fetal movement
- Inability to hold a conversation

---

## Integration with Strength & Nutrition

**Same-day strength + cardio:**
- Cardio comes **after** strength on combo days — don't compromise the strength stimulus with pre-fatigue
- Cap combo-day cardio at 15 min in Phase 1, 10 min in Phases 2–3

**Fuelling cardio:**
- Steady-state sessions under 30 min: no special fuelling, just normal pre-session meal 1.5–2 hr out
- Sessions over 30 min or any interval work: 20–30g carbs in the 30–60 min before
- Always carry water + a carb source (dates, banana, sports drink)
- On dedicated cardio days, add ~150 kcal to her intake (mostly carbs)

**Sweat and electrolytes:**
- Pregnancy increases sweat rate
- Add a pinch of sea salt to her water bottle on cardio days
- If sessions exceed 30 min or it's warm, use a proper electrolyte mix (sodium 300–500 mg, potassium, magnesium)

---

## Postural & Pelvic Floor Considerations

As the pregnancy progresses, the centre of mass shifts, lumbar lordosis increases, and the pelvic floor takes more load. Cardio choices should reflect this:

- **Incline walking > flat walking** — reduces low-back compression and engages glutes
- **Bike seat height and position matter** — she may need to raise the handlebars and shorten reach as the belly grows
- **Elliptical stride** — keep it shorter, more upright

## What "Core" Means in Pregnancy

The pregnant core is not just "abs." It's a **canister system**: diaphragm on top, pelvic floor on the bottom, transverse abdominis and obliques on the sides, multifidus at the back. All four walls have to coordinate, and during pregnancy this system is under continuous load and stretch from the growing uterus.

The goal is **not** to "keep the six-pack" or fight the rectus separation that naturally happens — diastasis recti to some degree is normal and expected (around 100% of women have it by the third trimester; it's a feature, not a failure). The goal is to keep the system **coordinated, responsive, and able to manage pressure** so that it bounces back postpartum.

## The Two Rules That Govern Everything

**1. No exercises that cause doming or coning of the abdomen.**
If you watch her midline during a movement and see the rectus push forward into a ridge or dome, that movement is creating more intra-abdominal pressure than her connective tissue can manage. Regress or remove it. This is the single most important visual cue you have.

**2. No exercises that load the rectus abdominis in a shortened position.**
Crunches, sit-ups, V-ups, hanging leg raises, toes-to-bar, jackknives — all out. They actively worsen diastasis and train the wrong pattern for what her body needs.

## What's In, What's Out

**Green light:**
- Anti-extension work (planks, dead bugs — with caveats below)
- Anti-rotation work (Pallof presses, anti-rotation holds)
- Anti-lateral flexion (suitcase carries, side planks)
- Breathing-coordinated bracing
- Pelvic floor work (Kegels done correctly, plus reverse Kegels)
- Hip-dominant work that incidentally trains the deep core (single-leg RDLs, bird dogs)
- Loaded carries

**Yellow light (assess weekly, regress as needed):**
- Front planks — fine in Phase 1, regressed to incline or hands-elevated in Phase 2, often dropped in Phase 3
- Dead bugs — watch carefully for doming, regress range of motion as needed
- Side planks — modify to knees, then to side-lying clams as needed

**Red light:**
- Crunches, sit-ups, any flexion-based ab work
- Hanging leg raises, toes-to-bar
- Russian twists with rotation under load
- Ab wheel rollouts (massive anti-extension demand — too much by trimester 2)
- Supine dead bugs after week 16 if held long
- Heavy Valsalva-braced lifts (this is core work whether we call it that or not)

## Daily Foundation: Breathing & Pelvic Floor (5 min, every day)

This is the non-negotiable baseline. Five minutes, every day, ideally morning and pre-bed. It's the most important "core work" she'll do.

**360° diaphragmatic breathing — 2 min**
- Side-lying or seated upright
- Hands on lower ribs
- Inhale through nose, expand ribs in all directions (front, sides, back) — belly rises gently, not aggressively
- Exhale through pursed lips, ribs come down, gentle pelvic floor lift on the exhale
- 8–10 breaths

**Connection breathing with pelvic floor — 2 min**
- Same position
- Inhale: ribs expand, pelvic floor relaxes and descends slightly (this is the part most women miss)
- Exhale: ribs come down, pelvic floor gently lifts (think "lifting a blueberry with your vagina" — Julie Wiebe's cue)
- 8–10 breaths
- **The relaxation phase matters as much as the contraction.** A pelvic floor that can't relax can't push a baby out and can't recover properly postpartum.

**Reverse Kegel practice — 1 min**
- Focused relaxation and lengthening of the pelvic floor
- Critical for labour prep — she has to be able to let go, not just contract

This 5-minute practice is what wires her nervous system to manage pressure during lifts and to push effectively during labour. Don't skip it.

## Diastosis Monitoring

Check her midline every 2–3 weeks. Easiest method: have her lie on her side (not supine after week 16), fingers across the midline above and below the navel, perform a gentle head lift, feel for the gap.

- **Fingertip width and shallow:** Normal, expected, no concern.
- **2+ fingers wide with shallow depression:** Watch your programming, ensure no doming exercises slipped in.
- **Deep, soft, no tension at the midline ("squishy"):** Regress all plank-position work, increase breathing and connection work, flag to her OB.
- **Visible doming during any exercise:** Remove that exercise immediately.

The depth and tension matter more than the width. A 3-finger gap with good tension is fine; a 2-finger gap that feels like jelly needs attention.

- Doming or coning of the abdomen during any movement
- Downward pelvic floor pressure during lifts ("bearing down" sensation)

- Urinary leakage during any exercise (early signal to regress, not push through)
- Low back pain that emerges or worsens during core work
- Round ligament pain that doesn't resolve quickly

Any of these = regress, switch exercise, and check setup. Persistent issues = referral to a pelvic floor physiotherapist, which honestly every pregnant lifter should see at least once anyway.

## Why This Is a Hard No

At programme week 12, she's **32 weeks pregnant**. Testing a 1RM at 32 weeks pregnant violates multiple safety principles that aren't negotiable:

**1. Her OB cleared her for moderate strength training.**
That clearance does not extend to maximal attempts. A 1RM is, by definition, maximal effort. Running a 1RM under a "moderate strength" clearance is operating outside the scope of what her medical team approved. If something went wrong, you'd be the trainer who took a 32-week pregnant client to a true max against medical guidance. That's a professional and ethical problem regardless of outcome.

**2. Valsalva is unavoidable at a true 1RM.**
You cannot complete a genuine 1RM without breath-holding and intra-abdominal pressure spikes. Even highly trained lifters who try to exhale through a max attempt end up bracing hard. Intra-abdominal pressure spikes at 32 weeks risk pelvic floor damage, worsen diastasis, and create cardiovascular strain on a system already managing 40–50% increased blood volume and elevated resting HR.

**3. Relaxin is at peak levels.**
By 32 weeks, ligamentous laxity is maximal. Her SI joints, pubic symphysis, and spinal ligaments are at their most vulnerable. The injury that takes a non-pregnant lifter two weeks to recover from could take her months and affect her delivery.

**4. Form breakdown risk is qualitatively different.**
Her centre of mass has shifted, her base of support is altered, her balance is genuinely different than it was 12 weeks ago. A near-miss rep at 32 weeks isn't the same as a near-miss at baseline — the consequences cascade differently.

**5. Fetal considerations.**
Maximal effort creates significant blood pressure spikes and reduces uterine blood flow during the attempt. We don't have good data on what a true 1RM does to a third-trimester fetus because nobody runs that study. The absence of data is not permission.

**6. Phase 3 RPE cap is 5.**
We programmed Phase 3 at RPE 5 for legitimate physiological reasons — fatigue management, joint laxity, fetal demand, recovery capacity. Spiking from RPE 5 across the whole phase to RPE 10 in a single session isn't peaking, it's whiplash, and her tissues aren't prepared for it.

Here's a Week 12 that gives her something to **commit to and feel proud of** without crossing the lines that matter.

### Option 1: Rep PR Week (my recommendation)
Test **submaximal rep PRs at RPE 7 cap** on lifts where the rep range itself is the achievement. Not "how much can you lift" but "how well can you execute under pregnancy constraints."

**Week 12 Peak Session — Lower (Wednesday):**
- Goblet box squat — work up to a top set of **8 reps at RPE 7** with the heaviest weight she's used all pregnancy
- Trap bar RDL — top set of **8 reps at RPE 7**
- Single-leg RDL — top set of **8 reps/leg at RPE 7**

**Week 12 Peak Session — Upper (Friday):**
- Incline DB bench press (45°) — top set of **8 reps at RPE 7**
- Chest-supported row — top set of **10 reps at RPE 7**
- Half-kneeling landmine press — top set of **8 reps/side at RPE 7**

These are real, trackable PRs. "Heaviest goblet squat I did pregnant" is a legitimate athletic achievement. Film them. Log them. Frame them as benchmarks she'll return to postpartum.

### Option 2: Pregnancy Strength Benchmark Test
Build a fixed test battery she runs at the end of pregnancy and again at specific postpartum milestones (12 weeks postpartum, 24 weeks postpartum, 1 year). This turns Week 12 into the **start of a comeback arc**, not the end of a build.

Battery example:
- Goblet squat — max reps at a fixed load (e.g., 20kg) at RPE 7 cap
- Incline DB bench — max reps at a fixed load at RPE 7 cap
- Suitcase carry — distance at a fixed load
- Single-leg RDL — reps at a fixed load
- Bird dog — quality reps held for 3 sec each

She gets to chase those numbers postpartum. Much more motivating than a one-shot max attempt that compromises her safety.

### Option 3: Movement Quality Showcase
Film a "training day" of her best sets across the programme. Slow-tempo goblet squats, clean single-leg RDLs, controlled incline presses, sharp carries. The achievement is **technical mastery under pregnancy constraints**, which is genuinely impressive and a legitimate flex among serious lifters.

## What the Real Peak Looks Like

The actual peak event of this programme isn't a 1RM. It's **delivery**. The 12 weeks of training, breathing work, pelvic floor coordination, and lean mass maintenance all converge on labour and postpartum recovery. That's the meet she's training for.

Reframe it for her like this:

> "Week 12 isn't a max test — it's the dress rehearsal for the actual event, which is delivery and your comeback. We're going to test rep PRs at RPE 7 so you've got benchmarks to chase postpartum, and we're going to use Week 12 to lock in the breathing and pelvic floor patterns that are going to determine how labour goes and how fast you get back under a bar. The 1RM test happens postpartum — and based on how strong you are right now, it's going to be a hell of a number."

Advanced lifters respond well to this framing because it respects them as athletes managing a season, not as people being told they "can't."

## When She Can Test a True 1RM

Realistically: **6–9 months postpartum**, assuming uncomplicated delivery, full clearance from her OB and a pelvic floor physio, return-to-lifting progression completed, no leaking, no doming, no pelvic pain at submaximal loads. We can build that progression when the time comes.

---

If she pushes back hard on this — and some advanced lifters will — the line to hold is: "I'm not the person who's going to take a 32-week pregnant client to a true 1RM. That's not a coaching call I'll make. We can absolutely make Week 12 feel like an achievement, but not that way." That's a reasonable, professional, defensible position, and she'll respect you more for holding it than for caving to it.

Want me to build out the postpartum return-to-lifting progression now, with the 1RM test as the capstone? That gives her something concrete to look forward to and a clear roadmap from delivery to first true max attempt.

# Complete 12-Week Prenatal Strength, Cardio & Core Programme

**Client:** 30-year-old advanced lifter, 20 weeks pregnant at programme start (32 weeks at completion). OB-cleared for moderate strength training.

**Contraindications:** No supine work after week 16, no 1RM attempts, no contact sports.

---

## Programme Overview

This is a structured 12-week prenatal block that gradually deloads as pregnancy progresses while preserving the **identity and stimulus of advanced training**. Strength sessions run 4×/week. Cardio runs alongside (150–180 min/week). Core work is integrated into strength days plus 2 standalone sessions. Daily 5-minute breathing and pelvic floor practice underpins everything.

**RPE Caps:**
| | Compound lifts | Isolation/Machine | Cardio steady | Cardio intervals |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Phase 1 | 7 | 7 | 5–6 | 6 |
| Phase 2 | 7 | 8 | 5–6 | 7 |
| Phase 3 | 5 | 5–6 | 4–5 | None |

**Universal Rules:**
- Exhale on exertion. No Valsalva. Ever.
- No supine work beyond 30 seconds; minimum 15° incline, ideally 30°+
- Monitor midline for doming/coning every set — regress immediately if it appears
- Talk test on all cardio
- Core temp under 38.5°C
- 2–4 reps in reserve on all compound work — no true failure on anything compound
- Hydration: 3–3.5 L/day baseline, more on training days

**Stop Immediately For:**
Vaginal bleeding, fluid leak, contractions, dizziness, chest pain, calf swelling, headache, persistent abdominal doming, reduced fetal movement, urinary leakage during a lift.

---

## Daily Foundation (Every Day, 5 Minutes)

Done morning or pre-bed. Non-negotiable. This is the highest-ROI work in the entire programme.

1. **360° diaphragmatic breathing — 2 min.** Side-lying or seated. Inhale through nose, expand ribs in all directions. Exhale through pursed lips.
2. **Connection breathing with pelvic floor — 2 min.** Inhale: ribs expand, pelvic floor relaxes and descends. Exhale: ribs come down, pelvic floor gently lifts. Both phases matter equally.
3. **Reverse Kegel practice — 1 min.** Focused relaxation and lengthening of the pelvic floor. Direct labour prep.

# Complete 12-Week Prenatal Strength, Cardio & Core Programme

**Client:** 30-year-old advanced lifter, 20 weeks pregnant at programme start (32 weeks at completion). OB-cleared for moderate strength training.

**Contraindications:** No supine work after week 16, no 1RM attempts, no contact sports.

---

## Programme Overview

This is a structured 12-week prenatal block that gradually deloads as pregnancy progresses while preserving the **identity and stimulus of advanced training**. Strength sessions run 4×/week. Cardio runs alongside (150–180 min/week). Core work is integrated into strength days plus 2 standalone sessions. Daily 5-minute breathing and pelvic floor practice underpins everything.

**RPE Caps:**
| | Compound lifts | Isolation/Machine | Cardio steady | Cardio intervals |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Phase 1 | 7 | 7 | 5–6 | 6 |
| Phase 2 | 7 | 8 | 5–6 | 7 |
| Phase 3 | 5 | 5–6 | 4–5 | None |

**Universal Rules:**
- Exhale on exertion. No Valsalva. Ever.
- No supine work beyond 30 seconds; minimum 15° incline, ideally 30°+
- Monitor midline for doming/coning every set — regress immediately if it appears
- Talk test on all cardio
- Core temp under 38.5°C
- 2–4 reps in reserve on all compound work — no true failure on anything compound
- Hydration: 3–3.5 L/day baseline, more on training days

**Stop Immediately For:**
Vaginal bleeding, fluid leak, contractions, dizziness, chest pain, calf swelling, headache, persistent abdominal doming, reduced fetal movement, urinary leakage during a lift.

---

## Daily Foundation (Every Day, 5 Minutes)

Done morning or pre-bed. Non-negotiable. This is the highest-ROI work in the entire programme.

1. **360° diaphragmatic breathing — 2 min.** Side-lying or seated. Inhale through nose, expand ribs in all directions. Exhale through pursed lips.
2. **Connection breathing with pelvic floor — 2 min.** Inhale: ribs expand, pelvic floor relaxes and descends. Exhale: ribs come down, pelvic floor gently lifts. Both phases matter equally.
3. **Reverse Kegel practice — 1 min.** Focused relaxation and lengthening of the pelvic floor. Direct labour prep.

---

## Weekly Template (All Phases)

| Day | Session |
|---|---|
| Mon | Lower A + short cardio |
| Tue | Cardio (steady) + Standalone Core A |
| Wed | Upper A + short cardio |
| Thu | Cardio (intervals or steady) |
| Fri | Lower B + Standalone Core B |
| Sat | Upper B + short cardio |
| Sun | Active recovery (walk or swim) |

Mid-week "Press & Pull" mini-session optional in Phases 1–2 (e.g., Wednesday evening or Saturday). 20–25 min, runs alongside Wed/Sat sessions if she wants extra pressing volume.

---

# PHASE 1: WEEKS 1–4
### Pregnancy Weeks 20–23
**Focus:** Establish prenatal-adapted patterns, maintain strength baseline, build aerobic base.

### Lower A
- Goblet box squat (above parallel) — 4×6 @ RPE 7
- Trap bar RDL — 4×8 @ RPE 7
- DB reverse lunge — 3×8/leg
- Single-leg glute bridge — 3×10/leg
- Side plank — 3×30s/side

*Post-session: 15 min easy bike @ RPE 4*

### Upper A — Incline Bench Focus
- Incline barbell bench press (30°), rack safeties set — 5×6 @ RPE 7
- Chest-supported row — 4×8
- Incline DB bench press (45°) — 4×8 @ RPE 7
- Half-kneeling landmine press — 3×8/side
- Cable triceps pushdown — 3×12
- Pallof press — 3×10/side

*Post-session: 10 min elliptical cooldown*

### Lower B
- Front-foot-elevated split squat — 4×8/leg
- Hip thrust (shoulders on bench, neutral spine) — 4×8 @ RPE 7
- Step-up to box — 3×8/leg
- Hamstring curl (seated or standing) — 3×10
- Bird dog — 3×8/side

*Post-session: 15 min easy bike*

### Upper B — Overhead & Landmine Focus
- Standing landmine press — 4×6/side @ RPE 7
- Neutral-grip lat pulldown — 4×8
- Seated DB shoulder press — 4×8 @ RPE 7
- Single-arm DB row — 3×10/side
- DB lateral raise + rear delt fly superset — 3×12 each
- Dead bug (regress if doming) — 3×8/side

*Post-session: 10 min walk*

### Optional Mid-Week Press & Pull (20–25 min)
- Incline DB bench press — 3×10 @ RPE 6
- Cable row — 3×12
- Dips (assisted as needed) — 2 sets to RPE 7

### Phase 1 Cardio Schedule
| Day | Session |
|---|---|
| Mon | Lower A + 15 min easy bike (RPE 4) |
| Tue | 30 min steady incline walk @ RPE 5–6 + **Standalone Core A** |
| Wed | Upper A + 10 min elliptical |
| Thu | Intervals: 5 min warm-up, 6 × (2 min @ RPE 6 / 2 min @ RPE 3) on bike, 5 min cooldown |
| Fri | Lower B + 15 min easy bike + **Standalone Core B** |
| Sat | Upper B + 10 min walk |
| Sun | 30–40 min walk or easy swim @ RPE 3–4 |

### Phase 1 Standalone Core Sessions

**Core A (10–12 min):**
- 360° breathing — 2 min
- Half-kneeling Pallof press — 3×10/side
- Suitcase carry — 3×30s/side (heavy — RPE 7)
- Bird dog with pause — 3×6/side
- Tall-kneeling anti-rotation hold — 3×20s/side

**Core B (10–12 min):**
- Connection breathing — 2 min
- Side plank with hip lift — 3×8/side
- Cable anti-rotation press — 3×12/side
- Dead bug with breath coordination — 3×6/side (exhale as leg extends)
- Farmer carry — 3×40s

**Progression:** Add 1 rep or small load each week. RPE never exceeds 7 on compounds.

---

# PHASE 2: WEEKS 5–8
### Pregnancy Weeks 24–27
**Focus:** Maintain the *feeling* of hard training through density, tempo, and unilateral overload. Pressing volume rises. Isolation/machine RPE cap raised to 8.

### Lower A
**A1.** Heels-elevated goblet squat, 3-sec eccentric, 1-sec pause — 4×8 @ RPE 7
**A2.** Cable pull-through — 4×12 @ RPE 7
*Superset, 75s rest between rounds*

**B1.** Single-leg RDL (DBs, light support if needed) — 4×8/leg @ RPE 7
**B2.** Front-foot-elevated split squat — 4×10/leg @ RPE 7
*Superset, 90s rest*

**C.** Seated leg curl, 2-sec pause at peak — 3×12 @ RPE 8
**D.** Copenhagen plank regression — 3×25s/side

*Post-session: 15 min bike intervals (60s @ RPE 6 / 90s @ RPE 4) × 6*

### Upper A — Pressing Density
**A1.** Incline barbell bench (30°), 2-sec pause on chest — 4×6 @ RPE 7
**A2.** Chest-supported row, 1-sec pause — 4×10 @ RPE 7
*Superset, 90s rest*

**B1.** Incline DB bench press (45°), 3-sec eccentric — 4×8 @ RPE 7
**B2.** Single-arm half-kneeling lat pulldown — 4×10/side @ RPE 8
*Superset, 75s rest*

**C.** Machine chest press — 3×12 @ RPE 8 (push this one)
**D.** Cable triceps pushdown + DB lateral raise — 3×12 each, back-to-back @ RPE 8
**E.** Pallof iso-hold — 3×25s/side

*Post-session: 10 min elliptical @ RPE 5*

### Lower B
**A1.** Belt squat OR hack squat, 2-sec pause at bottom — 4×8 @ RPE 7
**A2.** Walking lunge (DBs) — 4×10/leg @ RPE 7
*Superset, 90s rest*

**B1.** B-stance hip thrust — 4×10/leg @ RPE 8
**B2.** Step-up to box, controlled descent — 4×8/leg @ RPE 7
*Superset, 75s rest*

**C.** Standing or seated leg curl — 3×12 @ RPE 8
**D.** Side plank with leg lift — 3×10/side (drop leg lift if doming)

*Post-session: 12 min bike @ RPE 5*

### Upper B — Overhead & Variety
**A1.** Seated DB shoulder press, 2-sec pause overhead — 4×8 @ RPE 7
**A2.** Neutral-grip pulldown — 4×10 @ RPE 8
*Superset, 75s rest*

**B1.** Half-kneeling single-arm landmine press — 4×10/side @ RPE 7
**B2.** Chest-supported T-bar row — 4×10 @ RPE 8
*Superset, 75s rest*

**C.** Swiss bar OR Smith incline press — 3×10 @ RPE 8
**D.** DB curl + overhead triceps extension — 3×12 each, back-to-back @ RPE 8
**E.** Standing cable anti-rotation — 3×10/side

*Post-session: 10 min elliptical*

### Optional Mid-Week Press Mini-Session
- Incline DB bench — 4×8 @ RPE 7
- Cable row — 3×12
- Dips (assisted as needed) — 3×8 @ RPE 7
- Tricep + lateral raise superset — 3×12

### Phase 2 Cardio Schedule
| Day | Session |
|---|---|
| Mon | Lower A + 15 min bike intervals (60s @ RPE 6 / 90s @ RPE 4) × 6 |
| Tue | 35 min mixed-modality steady @ RPE 6 + **Standalone Core A** |
| Wed | Upper A + 10 min elliptical @ RPE 5 |
| Thu | Intervals: 5 min warm-up, 6 × (90s @ RPE 7 / 2 min @ RPE 4), 5 min cooldown |
| Fri | Lower B + 12 min bike @ RPE 5 + **Standalone Core B** |
| Sat | Upper B + 10 min elliptical |
| Sun | 30 min swim or aquatic walking |

### Phase 2 Standalone Core Sessions

**Core A (12 min):**
- Connection breathing with pelvic floor — 3 min
- Suitcase carry — 4×30s/side (heavy — RPE 7–8)
- Half-kneeling Pallof press, 2-sec pause — 3×10/side
- Bird dog — 3×8/side
- Side-lying breathing — 1 min

**Core B (12 min):**
- 360° breathing — 2 min
- Tall-kneeling anti-rotation hold — 3×25s/side
- Incline plank (hands on bench) — 3×30s
- Pallof press with overhead reach — 3×8/side
- Farmer carry — 3×40s (push the load)

**Watch For:**
- Doming during dead bugs → regress to arms-only with breathing
- Coning during planks → switch to incline plank immediately
- Round ligament pain → shorten lever, reduce load
- Bike seat discomfort → switch to recumbent
- Reflux on incline bench → switch to seated DB press

---

# PHASE 3: WEEKS 9–12
### Pregnancy Weeks 28–31
**Focus:** Movement maintenance, labour-prep conditioning, postural support, fatigue management.

### Lower A
- Goblet squat to box (parallel or above) — 3×8 @ RPE 5
- Cable pull-through — 3×12
- DB step-up — 3×8/leg
- Seated leg curl — 3×12
- Deep squat hold (supported) — 3×30s

*Post-session: 10 min recumbent bike (RPE 4)*

### Upper A
- Incline DB bench press (45°) — 3×8 @ RPE 5–6
- Seated cable row — 3×12
- Half-kneeling landmine press — 3×8/side
- Machine chest press — 3×10
- Single-arm pulldown — 3×10/side
- Diaphragmatic breathing drills — 3×8 breaths

*Post-session: 10 min elliptical*

### Lower B
- Hip thrust (light load, focus on glute connection) — 3×10
- Single-leg glute bridge — 3×10/leg
- Wall sit — 3×30s
- Banded clamshells — 3×15/side
- Cat-camel — 3×8

*Post-session: 10 min walk*

### Upper B
- Seated DB shoulder press (light) — 3×10
- Chest-supported row — 3×10
- Machine chest press — 3×10
- Face pull — 3×15
- Band pull-apart — 3×15
- Side-lying breathing with pelvic floor coordination — 3×8

*Post-session: 10 min easy bike*

### Phase 3 Cardio Schedule
| Day | Session |
|---|---|
| Mon | Lower A + 10 min recumbent bike (RPE 4) |
| Tue | 30 min recumbent bike or aquatic walking @ RPE 4–5 + **Standalone Core A** |
| Wed | Upper A + 10 min elliptical |
| Thu | 30 min split bike/elliptical, all steady @ RPE 5 (no intervals) |
| Fri | Lower B + **Standalone Core B** |
| Sat | Upper B + 10 min easy bike |
| Sun | 30–40 min swim or walk @ RPE 3 |

### Phase 3 Standalone Core Sessions

**Core A (10 min):**
- Connection breathing with pelvic floor — 3 min
- Suitcase carry (moderate load) — 3×30s/side
- Half-kneeling Pallof press — 3×10/side
- Bird dog — 2×8/side
- Reverse Kegel practice — 2 min

**Core B (10 min):**
- 360° breathing — 2 min
- Tall-kneeling anti-rotation hold — 3×20s/side
- Side-lying clamshells — 3×15/side
- Standing Pallof press — 3×10/side
- Pelvic floor coordination breathing — 3 min

### Weeks 11–12 Specific Modifications
- Drop one set across all strength work
- Drop one cardio session if fatigue accumulates
- Drop standalone core to 1×/week if needed; keep daily breathing
- Add daily 10–15 min easy walks if tolerated
- Add 5–8 min mobility cool-down: hip openers, thoracic rotations, ankle work

---

# WEEK 12 PEAK: REP PR WEEK

**Not a 1RM test.** Submaximal rep PRs at RPE 7 cap on lifts she's used through the programme. Filmed, logged, and used as postpartum return benchmarks.

### Wednesday — Lower Peak
- Goblet box squat — work up to top set of **8 reps @ RPE 7** (heaviest goblet weight used all pregnancy)
- Trap bar RDL — top set of **8 reps @ RPE 7**
- Single-leg RDL — top set of **8 reps/leg @ RPE 7**

### Friday — Upper Peak
- Incline DB bench press (45°) — top set of **8 reps @ RPE 7**
- Chest-supported row — top set of **10 reps @ RPE 7**
- Half-kneeling landmine press — top set of **8 reps/side @ RPE 7**

These numbers become her **Pregnancy Strength Benchmark** — retested at 12 weeks postpartum, 24 weeks postpartum, and 1 year postpartum. The 1RM test happens 6–9 months postpartum, pending full clearance from her OB and a pelvic floor physio.
